clue.text: Get better name to replace vacuous catwalk model

indicators.note: the name letter is put in place of the catwalk letters within the phrase

parts.note: to pick up is to recover or get better

indicators.note: an empty catwalk keeps only its outside letters, the inside emptied out

explanation.surface: A fashion booker wants to swap a vapid catwalk model for a better name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous catwalk' leaves CK; in PICK UP, N 'to replace' that CK gives PIN UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a glamour model whose picture is pinned to a wall.

clue.text: Good artist finally securing very large advance

indicators.note: the good letters hold the size letters fast inside them

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is the crossword stock for good
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

indicators.note: the final letter of artist is taken

explanation.surface: A good painter, at last landing a huge advance payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' reads as praise of the artist but is the pious abbreviation; 'securing' wraps it round the outsize letters and 'finally' takes the artist's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea, to advance it as an argument.

clue.text: Drop off slate on the counter

indicators.note: counter here means running against, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to slate

explanation.surface: A slate falls from the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the counter' turns PAN backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep briefly, which is a nap.

clue.text: Sweat as some executive rips report up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the run is read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run concealed inside it

explanation.surface: An executive sweats as they tear up a damning report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ERIPSREP from the phrase and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is the formal word for to sweat.

clue.text: Laid back about bad press for broadcast

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the shuffled letters
laid read back to front, the word running backwards
bad suggests the letters of press are in a wrong state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A laid-back approach to some poor press coverage for a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAID into DIAL, which goes 'about' SPERS, the anagram of PRESS from 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast as a noun can mean a scattering, a dispersal of seed or news.

clue.text: Medic on the brink with last bit of paper — it's used to clean bottoms

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medic
a brink is an edge

indicators.note: only the final letter of paper is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor on the verge of reaching for the toilet paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger scoops silt and mud from the beds of rivers and harbours.

clue.text: Partners found parking charges steep with Sierra

indicators.note: to charge is to load, so the steep word is loaded with the parking letter

parts.note: to souse is to steep or soak in liquid
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Couples discover that parking fees are steep, Sierra included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' means is loaded with: SOUSE takes P to make SPOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses are married partners, husbands and wives.

clue.text: Key argument for legal arrangement

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: The main argument for a legal deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Escrow is a legal arrangement where a third party holds money until conditions are met.

clue.text: One who's stepping out

parts.note: stepping out suggests going out on the town, but here it is literal walking while asleep

explanation.surface: Someone going out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stepping out' sounds like dating; read literally it is walking about, unknowingly, at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A somnambulist walks while still asleep, quite literally stepping out of bed.

clue.text: Nan's struggling with Wordle — getting LAIRD

indicators.note: struggling letters are thrown about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Nan, with the apostrophe-s read as is, joining the clue

explanation.surface: Grandma flounders at the daily word game, and her answer is LAIRD.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make LAIRD look like a Wordle guess; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish estate owner, a landed proprietor.

clue.text: Perhaps Miss America has drink with the Queen before her round

parts.note: to sup is to drink
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A pageant winner has a drink with the monarch before her round.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss America is a Marvel Comics heroine, not the beauty queen the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss America is a costumed comic-book crime fighter, one example of the type.

clue.text: Guilt-free bacon, essentially without fat

indicators.note: the essence, the central letter, of bacon is taken

parts.note: lean meat is meat without fat

explanation.surface: Lean bacon, eaten without guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means innocent, with no criminal record or guilt.

clue.text: Ultimately confident PIN number opens security for temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the number comes first, opening the answer

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: only the very last letter of confident is used

parts.note: a peg is a pin

explanation.surface: A PIN number gives security for short-term lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN in capitals looks like a bank code; read it as a pin, PEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg secures a tent, the classic temporary shelter.

clue.text: Note to justify ousting leader — and bring under government control

indicators.note: the leading letter is thrown out

parts.note: to rationalise is to justify with reasons

explanation.surface: A memo justifying a sacked boss, before a takeover by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting leader' takes the R off RATIONALISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nationalise an industry is to take it into state ownership.

clue.text: Small firm periodically repair old sign

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: letters taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A small business occasionally fixes an old sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes RPI from repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Leaves war secrets out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone walks away, and wartime secrets come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercress is a salad plant eaten for its leaves.

clue.text: Exam with a fifty-fifty at the start — it's bland and unoriginal

indicators.note: these letters stand at the beginning, before the exam word

parts.note: two fifties, each the Roman numeral L
an exam is a paper

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant uses a fifty-fifty lifeline right at the start of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty-fifty' looks like the quiz lifeline; it is two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallpaper is used figuratively for bland background music or art, unremarkable filler.

clue.text: Knock back Venture Sea Scout's terms

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so each word's final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A Venture Sea Scout rejects the conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' suggests rejecting; here it means to consume.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back food or drink is to eat or swallow it quickly.

clue.text: Beginning French for example

definitions.meaning: ... French is a British comedian, so ... is an example forename

explanation.surface: Starting with French, say, as a language lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like the language; it is Dawn French, the British comic actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The dawn of an era is its start; the comedian supplies the second sense.

clue.text: Artist following the right instrument

indicators.note: the artist's name comes after the other pieces

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: A painter follows the correct instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The theremin is an electronic instrument played without touching it.

clue.text: Face King John first

indicators.note: the toilet word comes first, ahead of the king letter

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Confronting King John before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: King John looks like one monarch; split it into K and the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that looks south faces south, so to look is to face.

clue.text: After long boring hours, Swedish company's wanting a rule for one who enjoys free movement

indicators.note: the furniture-firm part comes after the hours part
boring into means going inside, between the two hour letters

parts.note: H is short for hour, doubled for hours
to itch for something is to long for it

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: IKEA is a Swedish furniture company

explanation.surface: After hours of tedious waiting, a Swedish firm needs a rule on free movement of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means drilling into; 'wanting a' means the furniture firm loses its letter A, and 'After' places that part second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitchhiker travels free by thumbing lifts from passing drivers.

clue.text: I see diver returning dangerous water feature

parts.note: said aloud, see is the letter C

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the bird is read backwards

parts.note: the grebe is a diving bird

explanation.surface: Spotting a diver come back up near a dangerous water feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' is a bird, the GREBE, which 'returning' turns to EBERG.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a floating mass of ice, a hazard to shipping.

clue.text: Prisoner drinking a pint with international legend

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the prisoner word holds the rest

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A convict downs a pint alongside a sporting legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' looks like a famous person; here it is the text under a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the explanatory text under a picture, which is a caption.

clue.text: Pilot lowering an echo over sound system

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering moves a letter further down the word

parts.note: to pilot is to steer
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A pilot descends to hear an echo over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowering' moves one E of STEER down a place, giving STERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a hi-fi, a home sound system.

clue.text: Soft toy rabbit

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
a rattle is a baby's toy

explanation.surface: A cuddly toy bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit is British slang for to chatter on, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork', talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on and to prattle both mean to chatter idly.

clue.text: Sandwich, maybe with fish for show

parts.note: Sandwich is a port town in Kent
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish sandwich for a display.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich, with its capital, is a historic port in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to show or depict.

clue.text: In audition, why chat about craft?

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, why is the letter Y

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: At an audition, someone asks why they are chatting about arts and crafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHAT to ACHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is a boat or vessel, and a yacht is one.

clue.text: Run current inside 24 having forgotten charger earlier

indicators.note: the run and current letters are placed within what remains
forgotten means left out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the answer to 24 across
a charger is a large serving plate or tray
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A runner with current inside forgets to charge earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: A charger is a large serving plate; 'having forgotten' drops it from the 24 answer, leaving POR, and 'inside' places the run and current letters within.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means coming before in time.

clue.text: Mysterious comic — ace timing

indicators.note: comic as an adjective means absurd or jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inscrutable comedian with brilliant timing.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means puzzling or hard to fathom.

clue.text: Unwrap present for dog

indicators.note: unwrapping removes the outer covering, the letters at each end

parts.note: to stage a play is to present it

explanation.surface: Opening a gift for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwrap' strips S and E from STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, to tag along.

clue.text: Music producer concerning journalist ahead of publication

indicators.note: these letters come before the publication word

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ED is short for editor, a journalist
an organ is a newspaper or journal

explanation.surface: A record producer complains about a journalist before release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a person; it is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ is a keyboard instrument, a harmonium, which produces music.

clue.text: Dark endings hit occasionally

indicators.note: only some letters, every other one, are taken

explanation.surface: Bleak finales strike every now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness, so dark serves as a noun for it.
